title: HR Benefits Assistant gives anonymous internet users access to HR-Confidential via maker credentials
risk_statement: Because agent-hr-benefits is published to the public website with no user authentication and reads employee records through a SharePoint connection that runs with its maker's credentials, any anonymous internet user could query the agent to retrieve Highly Confidential HR content, resulting in a personal-data breach with regulatory, legal and reputational consequences.
likelihood_rationale: Internet-facing and anonymous; shortest attack path in the model (2 hops); no attacker effort beyond chatting; no compensating control evidenced.
impact_rationale: HR-Confidential is labelled Highly Confidential and critical; maker credentials bypass per-user access checks. Breadth is one site in the model; wider reach of the maker's own access is not evidenced.
recommended_action: CONTAINMENT by 2026-11-16 (2 business days): remove the public website channel or switch on Entra ID authentication. STRUCTURAL FIX by due date: replace the maker-credential connection with end-user (delegated) authentication; give the agent a dedicated Entra agent identity; confirm business need (no activity for 50 days) and unpublish if not needed.

risk_statement: Because agent-helpdesk runs as ai-helpdesk-01 holding the Entra Helpdesk Administrator role, offers password-reset and unlock tools to any authenticated employee in Teams, and no caller verification or approval step is evidenced, a malicious insider or a compromised employee account could instruct the agent to reset another user's password, resulting in account takeover and onward access to that user's data (in the model, critical payroll storage via user-dana).
assets: agent-helpdesk; ai-helpdesk-01; bp-itops; role-helpdesk-admin; user-dana; st-payroll
likelihood_rationale: Reachable by every authenticated employee, so any one compromised account suffices; generative orchestration with a direct reset tool; no caller verification, human approval or guardrail evidenced.
impact_rationale: Directory role allows reset of non-admin users; modelled reach is one user leading to critical payroll storage (blast-radius score 20). Breadth beyond user-dana is not modelled.
recommended_action: Remove the standing Helpdesk Administrator role from ai-helpdesk-01 or scope it with an administrative unit. Limit the reset tool to the authenticated caller's own account, or require target-user re-verification and human approval for resets of others. Log and alert on agent-initiated resets. Confirm where the bp-itops credential is stored.

title: Tenant-wide read grants on finance agent identities, reachable by prompt injection via invoice email (PROVISIONAL)
risk_statement: Because ai-invoice-01, the identity agent-invoice runs as, holds application Mail.Read on all mailboxes (incl. CFO) and Sites.Read.All on all sites (E-43), and sibling identities under the same blueprint hold one of these each (ai-invoice-02: Mail.Read; ai-expense-01: Sites.Read.All; E-44, E-45), and agent-invoice autonomously processes untrusted external email (E-13), an external sender could use indirect prompt injection to make the agent read mail or documents far beyond the invoices mailbox, resulting in exposure of confidential executive and finance data to the agent's context and any output channel it has. ASSUMPTIONS (not evidenced): (a) the Read mail / Search SharePoint tools accept arbitrary mailboxes and sites; (b) a disclosure channel exists (e.g. Post to ERP API, see R-12).
likelihood_rationale: Untrusted external email is processed autonomously with generative orchestration on, and sending an email takes minimal effort. Scored 3, not 4, because tool scope and a disclosure channel are not evidenced. Assumption: no guardrail or approval step (not evidenced; see R-09). Re-score when tool-scope and R-09 evidence arrives.
impact_rationale: Grants are app-only and tenant-wide over two critical assets (all mailboxes incl. CFO; all SharePoint sites); tool blast-radius score 35, or 39 if the blueprint credential leaks.
recommended_action: Limit mail access to the invoices shared mailbox (Exchange Online RBAC for Applications or an application access policy) and replace Sites.Read.All with Sites.Selected on the Finance site. EVIDENCE REQUEST: where the Mail.Read / Sites.Read.All grants are assigned (the model labels them 'inherited from blueprint' but places them on each child identity, E-46), and the scope of the Read mail / Search SharePoint tools. IF the grants are assigned at blueprint level, stop granting high-privilege permissions there and evaluate a separate blueprint per workload. Add prompt-injection defences.

title: DevOps Copilot holds standing Contributor and run-command power over production
risk_statement: Because the DevOps Copilot runs as mi-agent-devops with standing Contributor on rg-production and offers Run command on VM and Azure Resource Manager tools, a stolen developer session or manipulated agent instructions could drive the agent to run code on or change production resources, resulting in compromise of the payroll database VM and production disruption.
likelihood_rationale: Entry needs a stolen Teams session or Foundry project access (assumed-breach node); on-behalf-of user authentication adds some binding. But the agent is the top choke point (6 of 11 paths) and no approval step is evidenced.
impact_rationale: Contributor over production including the critical payroll DB VM; largest blast radius in the model (12 nodes, 4 critical, score 74).
recommended_action: Remove standing Contributor; use just-in-time elevation (PIM for Azure resources) or a least-action custom role. Require human approval for Run command and other write actions. Separate read-only diagnostic tools from change tools. Require phishing-resistant MFA and a compliant device for developer access to the agent.
